analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. Nothing here changes executable code, so no control, key handling or authorization path is modified in this PR.

Examined behavior described by the docs:
- Served-speed records (lines ~4592-4608) gain `serving` and `tensorAssistant` fields. Plans and the router use only records served the same way. The records sit in owner-only `~/.darkbloom/cluster/served-speed.json`. They hold timing and build SHA-256 values, with no prompt content or key material. This is local placement and routing telemetry, so it does not touch A-001 or the coordinator-to-provider trust boundary TB-002.
- Gemma tensor-parallel doc edits (lines ~4805-4808, 4866-4891) add a `--layer-stride` diagnostic option for tp-check and describe one-ahead decode pipelining. The pipelining text covers sampler draws and stop semantics, including a possible extra streamed token when a peer stops. These are performance and correctness notes. They do not alter the sealed all-sum collectives or the keyed, authenticated data plane.
- The docs say Gemma prefix caching in tensor parallel uses the SSD tier (`Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix`). That falls under the existing T-041 posture: HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL and per-account cacheSalt. Nothing here claims that the TTL, the lookup-tag derivation or the AAD changed, so the T-041 mitigations appear unaffected. Whether the code matches these docs was not reviewable, because no source was supplied.
- The patch excerpt is truncated, and the range map lists further changed head ranges (~6725 onward) outside these units. Those are not covered here.

No regression or new attack surface was identified from the supplied evidence. Residual question for integration: confirm that the Gemma TP prefix SSD tier reuses the existing cacheSalt and HMAC scoping. No source was supplied to check this.
